chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever upon whom the bounties are magnified, the provision of the people becomes heavy upon him; so if he stands with their provision, he attracts an increase of the bounties upon him from Allah, and if he does not do so, he has exposed the bounty to its removal.
ai.seo_question: How does generosity towards people affect the stability of divine blessings?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the dynamic nature of divine favor (ni'mah), linking its preservation to the believer's active management of social obligations (ma'unah). This teaching underscores the Shia concept that wealth is not merely personal property but a trust requiring circulation through generosity to prevent stagnation and loss, thereby aligning material sustenance with spiritual responsibility.
